correctness.rationale: The Dirichlet covariance is inverted on the simplex tangent hyperplane to reconstruct the affine reproducing kernel. Convexity of its absolute integral reduces the exact sharp norm to a vertex; a beta marginal and one sign split yield the incomplete-beta identity. An independent Beta--Gamma product coupling yields an error of at most sqrt(na+1)/n, and beta fractional moments plus Stirling estimates prove the two regimes for every parameter sequence. Critical hypotheses, endpoints, and the boundedness equivalence were checked analytically; the supplemental checker corroborates finite cases without substituting finite experiments for proof.

value.rationale: The Dirichlet family is a natural and widely used continuum of probability weights for simplex least-squares approximation; total concentration controls whether high-dimensional affine projection amplifies bounded signals by an O(1) factor or diverges. The theorem gives an exact computable stability constant, a dimension-uniform quantitative gamma surrogate, and a complete high-dimensional concentration threshold, beyond routine evaluation of one chosen weight. It also recovers the known uniform simplex benchmark as a consistency check rather than claiming that special case as new.
